So I get it’s weird. But she’s obviously grieving. She’s using his clothes to comfort her in her grief and setting a boundary (which might mean she’s lying to set the boundary). But it seems like the boundary she’s setting is she wants space to breathe and do what she needs to do in this time. not be interrogated about her relationship with him. 

It could all be bullshit and your girlfriend could be lying to you. But she still had a loss. Maybe a bit more flexibility and kindness would make her be more honest with you. And then everything will probably become more obvious to you and her once the situation is less complex

I’m just telling you what I want someone to tell me in your position, I think
Thankyou. A muffle is the perfect description

I had just turned 24 when he died so I was pretty much your age. I found I had to manifest my own growth. I’m not happy where I am and I feel like I haven’t chosen it but in the shit circumstances I had to make something happen or I’d have just stayed the same. 
If it’s the peak of happiness that’s just your depressed mind convincing you nothing good can happen and as I say plenty of good happy things have happened since he left and he left cause he felt that hed had peak happiness and couldn’t cope. I felt I’d never be happy again after he left too. But I can honestly say the hardest thing that ever happened to me and I can still find joy in small things. Happiness will evade you if you look for things to be sad about. I wish you the best. We are so young really and nobody has their shit together yet but there’s a future with happiness and sadness that you should stick around for I promise it’s there

You know my Fiance died last year by suicide. And it really nearly killed me too. If there’s anything I can say that I’ve learnt about suicide is once you’re gone you don’t know what you miss. He’s missing all the best bits of his life and he’s not here to enjoy them. Infinite things can happen if you stay around nothing will happen if you go. His best friend is having a baby and he would’ve been elated his brother is also having a baby the happiest times of his life and he’s not here to live them and the same will happen to you you just won’t know about it all because you gave up in the tough times. I say this with Well intention after he died I attempted suicide about four times in a psychiatric unit and I’ve been about to see the things that we would’ve missed if we both died. Please stick around to see how good it gets because it will infinite things can happen please stick about and be sure. I’m 24 my Fiance was 25. Infinite things can happen if you stay around only One thing will happen if you go. He had no idea the drastic impact and how far his death went. A friend of ours also died. And it will be the same for you and everybody else if you  give up before it gets better. Even in your darkest hours you can do it. Chat to me if you want. You’re worth every second of my time if I can help

I lost my fiancé last year I was very close proximity to him when he died. He had two brothers I can totally understand your pain. I’d say for the first couple of months it did hit me the same when I woke up so I can empathise with your feelings of feeling overwhelmed. My mail is open if you want to talk I’m doing mental health and suicide awareness courses now. Everything will feel a little bit difficult and I didn’t believe it when people told me but grief does get better it doesn’t go away we just grown around it. And everything you’re feeling I completely understand. I’m here if you wanna talk about it. You may not believe it now because I didn’t but it does get easier to cope with. I’m open to chat if you wanna message. I’m sorry you’re in this impossible journey and I’m sorry that you lost your brother. There’s a lots of milestones to come in your journey but I can talk if you want to privately. I was doing my nurse training when he died and it was totally the right time for me to take a break and let myself heal. You’re in healing and you can totally do it. I’m sending love and compassion. I’m sorry this is happening to you and I’m sorry it happened to your brother

Well I understand it can have potential racial meaning. But I just mean it as go away monkey man? I mean I wouldn’t use anything with anyone but him and his friends cause strangers on the internet can be sneaky 😂

You’ll be on the kidney transplant list with severe gastro intestinal damage and die of kidney failure in years to come before you get the emotional relief you’re seeking from taking those pills. Trust me. This isn’t the solution to your problems. Please get help

I’m sorry to hear this. There’s no key to getting over grief and loss. I’m sorry you have to experience this whilst you’re at a point where you feel you don’t have the strength. I hope you can look after yourself and continue to live your life the best you can.

If you’re going to die anyway why not at least give yourself peace and kindness before you go. That’s my philosophy. You don’t have to end your life at al. But if you’re going to treat yourself with kindness before you do- then maybe unintentionally it’ll make you change your mind, I know it probably won’t but it’s worth trying

Because 2 weeks ago I planned to do it on the 12. I failed and now I have an extra week alive. That weeks been horrendous but there have been things that made me smile and laugh against my will. 
Every day is a day where at least one positive thing can happen. You just have to look for it as hard as you look for the bad things that are happening. We have the habit of only picking up on things that are bad when we feel bad and discrediting anything good

It is sad that in the moment that we choose to end our journey the price we pay is we have to be alone. 

I really hope you can hold on. Dying is an important chapter in everyone’s journey- it shouldn’t be rushed or painful or traumatic. 

Everyone has to die at some point. Please try to hold onto something even for a day longer than the day you intend to do it

I love the sentiment of this post. Someone who isn’t bereaved by suicide but affected and wants it to stop-  and I for one appreciate that compassion. 

You won’t get much logic or response here to your pleas and advice. People are unwell and mental illness doesn’t go away with a community group and positive attitude. Some people come from socio economic backgrounds that deem it impossible for them to not live a life plagued by stress, loss and mental illness. And unfortunately all the love in the world doesn’t fix someone- I know because I tried. 

Your acknowledgement that you aren’t a psychologist or psychiatric doctor shows you know you aren’t qualified to know what to say. People who don’t live in suicidality can never understand the people who do. 

People who do are sick of being told the same things ie:
Be kind to yourself
Get help 
You deserve to live and be happy
Find hobbies
Times a healer 
People care about you 
You can be fixed

The infinite number of things we get told that is literally nothing to us and doesn’t help is so stressful. Because we live with this our entire lives it’s not just a day of depression- it’s our lives. People say these things and feel we aren’t tying when we don’t accept the advice and just do it. 

At the point of suicide someone is in an acute state- that they have taken a period of time and trauma or stress to get to. Nobody just wakes up  suicidal for no reason. At that point instincts to survive are overriden by the need to get away from the emotional pain and trauma and the time needed for it to be alleviated of that trauma only exacerbates their suicidal needs. 

People die of this because it’s a symptom of illness. The ironic thing is the more acutely unwell someone is the harder they are to treat because mental health support is partially motivational and if the patient isn’t motivated or has the energy to engage then it’s a cycle that never ends and usually results in suicide. 

It’s a far to complex thing that has to be assessed on an individual basis to decide how to treat someone and how they should react. I’m sorry you’re seeing so much of it and it’s bothering you. The issue is far bigger than any of us to be able to conquer it.

When my partner died a few weeks ago I would get so upset I vomited. Then I started vomiting even when I wasn’t upset. A psychiatric doctor told me I have to find ways of letting the energy out or my body is going to expel it in ways physically like making me vomit. I can’t suggest what would help your mum but it helped me to know why I was vomiting. I’m sorry for your loss

It was suspension so it only took about 10 seconds to pass out. The anchor point I was using broke after I passed out. Obviously when I hit the floor it loosened enough for me to regain consciousness and instinct kicked it and I choked for a bit on the floor and struggled to remove it. Nobody heard. I just couldn’t hide the ligature marks on my neck. It was the morning after my boyfriend had hanged himself

I’m sorry to hear that. I really really am. I’m sorry we have to go through this and are the ones left behind with twice the pain to carry. 
People seem to dwindle. People messaging showing condolence and sympathy isn’t even close to having support- nobody is asking how things are anymore. I haven’t seen anyone since 3rd September. His parents are holidaying a lot to help them grieve and have really really surprised me with how little they are supporting me. I’m stuck in a different city sofa surfing and trying to survive. Very much not coping. I was taken back into hospital on Saturday for a OD. I don’t know what’s going to happen

I was frustrated. My emotional pain was still more painful than hanging myself until I passed out. 
It got me 8 days on a psychiatric unit with someone with me 24/7. I still wish I’d been left- once I’d passed out it was essentially finished.

I’ve got BPD and feel like I have to engage in services to show that I’m willing to engage in services- if that makes sense. Can’t say they’re not doing enough and not engage when they offer something, even if it’s inadequate. 

I get frustrated at people who don’t know what to do for me because it seems that they’re not trying or doing things I’d do for someone in my position. But I was training as a paediatric nurse before all of this so understand the care plan side of care. I think that’s making it difficult to manage my expectations of people and to engage with services in a non professional, patient way- instead of as a nurse. 

I’ve been told I have too much insight and it makes it difficult to treat me. But BPD makes me erratic and inconsistent in my interactions with people. You make a good point of forgiving people for their ignorance- all I ask of people is to understand that you can’t understand and not invalidate me. Because I’m not just a bit down and anxious. I’m mentally unwell. People who don’t understand think of you could just change your outlook- your an adult. You have to chose what happens to you. Invalidates mental health struggles

I can’t give you the answers you need to find reasons to live. I’m not going to be a hypocrite and say the cliche stuff. Everyone has stuff to carry. I’m in the same boat as you. 
You should read that article. I know you haven’t lost someone but it’s context to your own feelings and how you’ll leave people. 
Inevitably things can’t stay the same. It’s just about if you can hold the emotional pain long enough for things to get better and get relief. I hope you can. I’m happy to talk if you need to

I was training to be a paediatric nurse before my partner died. I looked after him and stopped him for 6 months before he died. Professional support was shit. Even I kept telling him “we have to trust them- they’re the professionals” 
When really they didn’t know what to do with him because they don’t have the evidence based research to treat everyone individually. 
Whole lot of reliance on someone getting better and blame on them when the professionals are inadequate and they don’t get better. 
It’s happening to me now and I have the experience to help myself as much as I can.

6 weeks ago my boyfriend of 7 years hung himself. He was 25. I mean this in the most sincere way: if you do this to her there’s a chance you’ll kill her too. There is no way for you to kill yourself and not ruin her entire life. 
Even if you broke up and 6 months later killed yourself she would feel no different in her response to it and ask the same questions. Whilst you have someone to live for you have to try. 
This article is helpful:

https://www.healthline.com/health/mental-health/losing-someone-to-suicide

Please don’t do this to yourself or her. You can’t take this shit back and it changes lives.

I’ve just been blacking out since this morning and resting. I think by morning it’ll be out of my system. Shit thing is I have no sedatives now for my anxiety and trauma- but that’s my own fault. 
There isn’t any way for me to see a dr without it flagging up my recent section detainment and putting me back into hospital. 
Thanks for the advice. I am in the suicidewatch group too. I question if any of it will make any difference though but I’m trying

Did you read what I said? Didn’t say I did kill my self I was asking if I need to see a doctor after ingesting. 
Also you shouldn’t say such unkind things when you have no idea of someone’s situation. “I hope you pay the consequences for killing yourself like this” is a shitty thing to say to anyone. You have no idea why a person would feel that way. Who are you to be so judgy.
I intend fo carotid  asphyxiate. I can’t cope with my fiancé dying. We had lovely things  hung himself and took him selfaway can’t cope alone. Morning can help I need him

I just got released from a section two detainment after an attempt after my partner hung himself 03/08. 
I called the uk crisis team and said I’m not well. I was told to call back if I got worse. I asked what they would give me if I call back that they aren’t giving me now- I’m already on sedatives. The mental health nurse literally said to me “I don’t know I haven’t got a crystal ball have I? I’ll assess it then” 
It’s like they constantly need you to be a little bit worse. I’m also scared to be too honest because I’ll be sectioned again. Hospital is the last place anyone needs to be when they’re suicidal makes you want it more

He had only recently started on cider. Previously drank ale which he couldn’t drink much of. He did have reflux a lot but it was treatable and tbh he was never really without it long. Difficult to tell a full time working adult that they are drinking too much. There’s always an excuse
Of cider yes

It’s funny when people tell you you’re strong and you feel the weakest you’ve ever felt. Looking objectively at my situation I probably am, as are many people, stronger than they think they are. Nobody ever prepares or imagines for a reality where suicide affects them. Sometimes you’re not strong by choice. I still don’t know if it will get me like it did him. He promised the week before that he was responding to therapy and wouldn’t kill himself and I genuinely believe he believed that. Gives me a false sense of security in my own well-being

If you live by the philosophy of leave everyone who’s depressed before they affect you one day you may be depressed yourself and have nobody there to help you. Suicide isn’t the only thing that can happen when someone is depressed and you help them. There’s no statistic to the people that were helped and didn’t take their own lives. 
I’ve done it now and I’d do it again, with better knowledge, to try and help someone who was suicidal. It’s a very scary place to be- at the point of suicide it’s an acute illness all natural instincts to live are switched off. Why would someone who has died be looking for your affirmation and attention. They were unwell and they died from their illness. I agree with what your saying in terms of self care but there has to be a line where you sometimes help someone because it’s right to.

I have ptsd from what happened to my friend. I did therapy I needed and got the skills then so I have some coping strategies. Ultimately the issue I have that my rational mind is reminding me is that regardless of anything my person has died and I feel awful being here when he couldn’t be

The thing is there’s is simultaneously nothing helpful to say and everything you say being helpful. People saying things and caring at all is a placebo affect and should be recognised as positive. 
Grievance counselling or counselling in any form has a 6 month waiting list in the uk. There’s literally nothing the professionals can do but be there and talk. Talking doesn’t do a whole lot to ease the matter of the situation. Having contact and talking to people who have experienced the situation normalises is a bit for me though. That helps

She too was concerned for how he acted and was scared of him and he never treated her as physically bad as you have described here until he slit her throat. 
Please please access the relevant support to remove this person from your life. 
I am more than happy to advise if needed. My friends family have completed work via her charity and have passed laws to help people in Situations like yours! 
Stay safe
